chunks: But he who believes and does the right will have an excellent reward, and we shall make things easy for him.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Al-Jaza' Al-Hasna' and 'Yusra' in Surah Al-Kahf?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, 'Al-Jaza' Al-Hasna' is often interpreted as the ultimate reward of Paradise, while 'Yusra' (ease) signifies the divine facilitation of affairs for the faithful, particularly through the intercession of the Ahl al-Bayt. This verse underscores the inseparable link between belief (Iman) and righteous action (Amal Salih), a core tenet of Shia theology, promising that God will make the path to success smooth for those who adhere to this dual principle.
